digest.component_or_area: code-review impact model and gate routing
propositions: The code-v3 impact model discards the verifier's prod_impact and trigger_likelihood answers for the maintenance lane, preventing test-sufficiency findings from reaching the blocking threshold despite having substantive user-reach consequences.

A commit can simultaneously declare a contract (stale>0 allowed) and ship a test forbidding that exact state (stale=0 asserted), creating a contradiction that code-v3 review missed because the contract-contradicting-assertion antipattern is absent.

The code-v4 impact model must split the maintenance lane by binary consequence class and apply prod_impact-keyed damping to moderate-consequence binaries (×0.6 when prod_impact=none/low; ×1.0 when prod_impact=medium/high), while restricting the reversibility floor to consequence lanes only to prevent debt-only findings from false-positive blocking.

The tests finding class must become blocking@0.54 in packaged routing, with the new forbids_contract_allowed_state binary emitted only when both contract-allowed and test-forbidden states are present verbatim and deliberate tightening is not stated.

Stored code-v3 sidecars must never be rewritten or re-scored in place; new reviews emit code-v4 scores while existing code-v3 sidecars remain unchanged and missing-binary fields contribute 0 to scoring.

Replay of v3 → v4 transition against corpus (1881 sidecars, 1243 changes, 3384 findings) must verify zero demotions of currently-blocking findings, prod=none/low mass remains advisory, and impact scores remain grounded to recorded verifier answers for prod_impact and trigger_likelihood.
